data.name: Indra
data.long_meaning: Indra is the Hindu deity of rain, thunder, and storms. He is also considered as the king of gods and the god of war. He is often depicted riding a white elephant and carrying a thunderbolt.
data.numerology_meaning: Indra is a number 2 life path, which represents balance and harmony. Those with this life path are natural peacemakers and seek to bring harmony to their relationships and communities.

in_sanskrit.name: इन्द्र
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who possesses power, victory, holiness, bow, and wealth. The king of gods and the god of rain and thunder, Indra is revered as the god of strength and is invoked for success and victory.

vedic_reference.note: Indra is the king of gods and the god of rain and thunder in Hinduism. He is mentioned in the Rigveda and other ancient Hindu texts. He is considered the god of strength and is invoked for success and victory.

data.cultural_impact: Indra is an integral part of Hindu culture and deeply influences their daily lives. His presence is felt during monsoon seasons and festival celebrations like Teej, Shraavana and Raksha Bandhan, which are dedicated to him. He is often invoked through various rituals like "Indra Jalpukri" during agriculture to ensure better crop yield.
data.spiritual_significance: Indra, as a god, is considered to have a purifying effect. The sound of thunder, which is often associated with him, signifies the breaking down of old patterns and the renewal of energy. In Hindu philosophy, he represents the power of change, transformation, and destruction that is necessary for creation and renewal. He encourages us to embrace change and possesses the ability to clear obstacles and pave way for progress.

historical_references.reference: Indra is the god of thunder, rain, and storms in Hindu mythology. He is mentioned in the Rigveda (circa 1500 BCE), one of the oldest sacred texts in the world.
Indra is also considered the king of the gods in Hinduism and is depicted as having slayed the demon Vritra, who had been obstructing the flow of rivers, allowing the rains to flow freely.

modern_usage.modern_context: Indra is a prominent deity in Hindu mythology, often depicted as the king of the gods and the god of rain. He is a popular figure in Bollywood movies, with actors like Amitabh Bachchan and Anil Kapoor portraying him on screen. On social media platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and Reddit, fans of Hindu mythology and Bollywood discuss and share content related to Indra, including artwork, stories, and trivia.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Indra from Chennai, India embodies the meaning of Indra - "Lord of the Heavens". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Indra, the Vedic deity of rain, represents the dynamic, creative, and unpredictable power of nature. He is the giver of rains and the lord of the heavens, symbolizing strength, power, and leadership. His mythology revolves around the themes of victory and power, reflecting the human aspiration to harness and master the forces of nature.
